input.content:
You are an expert requirements engineer evaluating User Stories using the Quality User Story (QUS) framework by Lucassen et al.

Your task is classification, not rewriting. Judge ONLY the QUS criterion supplied in the task. Do not invent additional defect categories. Do not penalize stylistic preferences unless they are directly relevant to the supplied criterion.

Use the entire project backlog only when the supplied criterion requires set-level comparison or when contextual interpretation is explicitly necessary. When the criterion is story-level, assess each target story primarily from its own text.

For every target story, return exactly one binary decision:
- "Violation": the story violates the supplied QUS criterion.
- "No Violation": the story does not violate the supplied QUS criterion.

Also return concise evidence and rationale. For set-level criteria, list related story IDs when the decision depends on another story. Do not use "Uncertain" or "Insufficient Context" in model outputs: the Gold Standard may contain such labels, but these are excluded from the primary binary effectiveness metrics.

Return valid JSON only, with this shape:
{
  "evaluations": [
    {
      "story_id": "...",
      "criterion": "...",
      "decision": "Violation|No Violation",
      "evidence": "short text span or empty string",
      "rationale": "short criterion-specific justification",
      "related_story_ids": [],
      "confidence": "High|Moderate|Low"
    }
  ]
}

Every target story ID must appear exactly once. Do not add prose outside the JSON object.

QUS CRITERION
Name: Conflict-free
Dimension: Semantic
Scope: set
Definition: A user story is not inconsistent with another user story in the same specification.
Operational decision rule: Violation when two stories impose incompatible permissions, behaviors, constraints, states, or rules. Similarity alone is not a conflict.

PROMPTING CONDITION
One-shot: one worked example is provided below. The demonstration is synthetic and is not drawn from PlanningPoker, BADCamp, or Zooniverse.

WORKED EXAMPLE
Example 1:
Demo context:
DEMO-CF-A: As an editor, I want to edit any published article.
Target: DEMO-CF-B: As an editor, I want to edit only articles that I created.
Expected evaluation:
{"story_id": "DEMO-CF-B", "criterion": "Conflict-free", "decision": "Violation", "evidence": "edit only articles that I created", "rationale": "The target story restricts editing in a way that conflicts with DEMO-CF-A, which permits editing any published article.", "related_story_ids": ["DEMO-CF-A"], "confidence": "High"}

PROJECT
Zooniverse

FULL BACKLOG
ZO-001: As a user, I want to search and discover music using content identification or fingerprinting.
ZO-002: As a user, I want to search and discover music based on my profile.
ZO-003: As a user, I want to search and discover music based on other users similar to myself.
ZO-004: As a user, I want to search and discover music or ringback tones similar to a given music video based on content similarity.
ZO-005: As a user, I want to search and discover music by exploiting enriched metadata and image tags, so that I find related artists, new genre, or other relevant listening path.
ZO-006: As a user, I want to upload tagged videos and have tags available for all further processing steps.
ZO-007: As a user, I want to view thumbnail sequences of video segments.
ZO-008: As a user, I want to get info about similar video items and segments.
ZO-009: As a user, I want to get info about perceptually similar video items and segments.
ZO-010: As a user, I want to receive content recommendations from similar profiles.
ZO-011: As a user, I want to receive content recommendations based on most relevant news events in my area.
ZO-012: As a user, I want to identify persons in videos, and receive related information about them.
ZO-013: As a user, I want to identify products in videos, and receive related information about them.
ZO-014: As a user, I want to identify broadcaster logos in videos, and receive related information about them.
ZO-015: As a user, I want to identify brands in videos, and receive related information about them.
ZO-016: As a user, I want to take a picture or upload an image, so that I am recommended with videos related to that picture or image.
ZO-017: As a user, I want to walk around, access content using a geographical map and be informed if there are videos covering the area, monuments or any other relevant point of interest.
ZO-018: As a user, I want to search content items using automatic speech recognition.
ZO-019: As an admin, I want to see, validate and edit segmentation of videos.
ZO-020: As an admin, I want to annotate news video segments and extract a topic for each segment.
ZO-021: As an admin, I want to filter and rank videos based on A/V quality aspects.
ZO-022: As an admin, I want to get a quick assessment of whether audio material has been edited before the upload.
ZO-023: As an admin, I want to prefilter nudity content.
ZO-024: As an admin, I want to prefilter content using search based on low­level asset information.
ZO-025: As an admin, I want to automatically validated the ingested contents for copyright infringement.
ZO-026: As an admin, I want to prefilter the content using search on high­level asset information such as metadata and tags either recognized by the system of provided by the user.
ZO-027: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to assess how interesting or appealing or complex a picture is based on automated analysis, citizen annotations, and comments on Talk.
ZO-028: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to detect when a scientist should be prompted to look at a subject, based on annotations and information from Talk comments.
ZO-029: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to identify volunteer types.
ZO-030: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to preclassify the Galaxy Zoo images using simple low­level image features.
ZO-031: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to automatically detect Snapshot Serengeti images with no classifiable animals in them.
ZO-032: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic image series detection for the case of timestamping malfunction in Snapshot Serengeti images.
ZO-033: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic animal species preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti.
ZO-034: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic animal attribute preclassification in Snapshot Serengeti.
ZO-035: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic animal number detection in Snapshot Serengeti.
ZO-036: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic segmentation or localization of plankton in Plankton Portal.
ZO-037: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to automatically detect Plankton Portal images with no classifiable plankton in them.
ZO-038: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic detection of plankton size or orientation in Plankton Portal images.
ZO-039: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic preclassification of plankton species in Plankton Portal images.
ZO-040: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform automatic worm motion analysis to reduce video duration in Worm Watch Lab.
ZO-041: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to automatically detect the time in a Worm Watch Lab video where the worm lays an egg.
ZO-042: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to detect important features such as areas of flooding, damage, temporary shelters, blocked roads etc in the satellite images.
ZO-043: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to assess the probability/weight of a volunteer’s classification based on their experience.
ZO-044: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to perform prefiltering of the images to remove artefacts such as bright stars and camera read errors.
ZO-045: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to detect moving and transient objects in the images.
ZO-046: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to remove background noise and distracting sounds from the audio files.
ZO-047: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to group whale calls that are similar.
ZO-048: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to identify the number of whales heard in a single audio file.
ZO-049: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know when I should interrupt a volunteer.
ZO-050: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know whether I should interrupt a volunteer with text, an image, or a video.
ZO-051: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know when I should educate a volunteer.
ZO-052: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know whether I should educate a volunteer with text, an image, or a video.
ZO-053: As a Zooniverse admin,I want to know which piece of education I should give to a volunteer.
ZO-054: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know when a volunteer has made an interesting comment on a subject.
ZO-055: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know when Zoonibot should comment on a subject.
ZO-056: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know when Zoonibot should give an explanation.
ZO-057: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to know what Zoonibot should say to a volunteer.
ZO-058: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to group subjects by similarity.
ZO-059: As a Zooniverse admin, I want to recommend different projects to volunteers based on their previous experiences.
ZO-060: As an admin, I want to see a summary of articles, so that I reuse them.

TASK
Evaluate EVERY story in the backlog for the single criterion "Conflict-free".
Do not evaluate any other QUS criterion in this call.
If the criterion is set-level, compare stories across the full backlog and identify related story IDs when relevant.
If the criterion is individual-level, do not treat a problem belonging solely to another QUS criterion as evidence for this criterion.
Return exactly 60 evaluation objects, one for each story ID.
